reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item: they give the six-month deadline counted from the Social Security alta, say it has likely lapsed, describe the regime correctly and recommend checking the vida laboral and seeing an asesor fiscal. B cites the correct regulation article (Art. 116 RIRPF), adds that the deadline can also run from a home-country Social Security coverage certificate, and adds practical points (the Modelo 720 obligation, the Madrid new-resident incentive, the risk of 24% withholding being clawed back). A cites the wrong regulation article (119), though it hedged that citation, and it adds a useful Art. 7.p pointer; on balance B is slightly more precise and complete.

A: Attributes the Modelo 149 six-month deadline to Art. 119 RIRPF; the provision is Art. 116 RIRPF (hedged as from memory)
B: Combined marginal rate at 140,000 EUR in Madrid given as about 45%; it is closer to 43% (22.5% state + 20.5% Madrid), though hedged as approximate
